parts.article:
The Origin of Paper
 
(A) The word paper derives from the Greek term for the ancient Egyptian writing material called papyrus. In about 2400 BC, the Egyptians discovered how to make a writing surface out of papyrus, a type of reed that grows along waterways in southern Europe and North Africa. The Egyptians cut the plant into strips which they softened in water. Papyrus was cross-woven into a mat and then pounded into a hard, thin sheet.
 
(B) As the papyrus plant requires subtropical conditions to grow, papyrus was not much used in Europe at that time; instead, the main material used for writing was parchment. This was made from animal skin and was extremely expensive. In fact, it has been estimated that a single book written on parchment required the skins of 300 sheep. The skins had to be specially prepared by drying them and they were then stretched on a special frame. It is not known when parchment was first introduced, but it was the main writing material in Europe for hundreds of years.
 
(C) Paper—made from pulp, rags and fibres of plants—seems to have been invented in China and is considered to be one of the Four Great Inventions of Ancient China. In 105 AD, under the Han-Dynasty emperor Ho-Ti, a government official in China named Ts'ai Lun was the first to start a papermaking industry. Ts'ai Lun seems to have made his paper by mixing finely chopped mulberry bark and hemp rags with water, mashing the mixture flat with a stone mortar, and then pressing out the water and letting it dry in the sun. He may have based his idea on bark cloth, which was very common in China and also made from mulberry.
 
(D) Previously, during the Shang (1600-1050 BC) and Zhou (1050-256 BC) dynasties of Ancient China, documents were ordinarily written on bone or bamboo (on tablets or bamboo strips bound and rolled together into scrolls), making them very heavy and awkward to transport. The light material of silk was sometimes used, but was normally too expensive to consider. When paper was first invented, it was used for purposes of wrapping or padding protection for delicate bronze mirrors. Although paper for writing became popular by the 3rd century AD, it continued to be used for wrapping and other purposes. During the Tang Dynasty (618-907 AD) paper was folded and sewn into square bags to preserve the flavour of tea. During the same period, according to a written account, tea was served from baskets with multi-coloured paper cups and paper napkins of different sizes and shapes. During the Chinese Song Dynasty (960-1279 AD) not only did the government produce the world's first known printed paper money, or banknote, but paper money bestowed as gifts was wrapped in special paper envelopes.
 
(E) Paper spread widely outside China; other Asian cultures, even after seeing paper, could not make it themselves. Instruction in the manufacturing process was required, and the Chinese were reluctant to share their secrets. It made its true push westward in 751 AD when the Tang Dynasty was at war with the Islamic world. During a battle on the banks of the Talas River, a Chinese caravan was captured which happened to include several papermakers. They were taken away to Samarkand, which was a good place to make paper because it had an abundant supply of hemp and flax. Samarkanders changed the technology of manufacturing paper. They began to prepare it in stone mills and Samarkand became an important papermaking centre. The rudimentary and laborious process of papermaking was refined, and bulk manufacturing of paper began in Iran, where they invented a method to make a thicker sheet of paper, which helped transform papermaking from an art into an important business. Gradually papermakers made their way further west through the Arab world—to Baghdad, Damascus and Cairo. Finally, when the Moors from North Africa invaded Spain and Portugal, they brought the technology with them and so it was that papermaking entered Europe in the 12th century.
 
(F) In Europe, the preferred medium for the artists and literati of the time was still the smooth and lustrous parchment. The notion of paper being used as a practical everyday item did not occur until the 15th century, when Johannes Gutenberg perfected movable-type printing, which included the use of metal moulds and alloys, a special press, and oil-based inks, allowing the mass production of printed books. The birth of the modern paper and printing industry is commonly marked from this date. Printing technology rapidly developed and created an ever-increasing demand for paper. The early European papers were made from recycled cotton and linen—and a huge trade quickly developed around the trading of old rags. It is said that the disease known as the Black Death entered England from Europe on these old rags. Yet soon this source became insufficient and some curious attempts were made to find new materials. Experiments with fibres such as straw, cabbage, wasp nests and finally wood resulted in inexpensive—and replaceable—materials for papermaking. Today, the long, soft fibres of softwoods such as spruce have become the most suitable source of pulp for the mass production of paper.
parts.questions:
Questions 1 – 7
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 1-7 on your answer sheet, write:

Q1 In Ancient China, writing was occasionally done on silk.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q2 Coloured paper was invented during the Tang Dynasty.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q3 Papermakers from Samarkand were captured by the Chinese.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q4 Papermaking as a large-scale industry originated in Iran.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q5 Papermaking skills were brought to Europe via North Africa.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q6 When Gutenberg invented movable type, paper materials were very expensive.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q7 The end of the trade in rags was brought about by the difficulty of transporting them.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

reference:
Q1

干扰 题目中的“occasionally”对应原文的“sometimes”，不要因为后面说“too expensive”而忽略了它确实被使用过的事实。

句子 (Paragraph D) “The light material of silk was sometimes used, but was normally too expensive to consider.”

解析 题目说在中国古代，书写偶尔（occasionally）是在丝绸上进行的。原文D段提到丝绸这种轻便材料“was sometimes used（有时被使用）”，意思一致，选 TRUE。

Q2

解析 原文D段虽然提到唐代使用了“multi-coloured paper cups（多彩纸杯）”，但并没有说彩色纸是在唐代“发明（invented）”的，信息缺失，选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 文中只提到了“使用”了彩色纸制品，不要把“使用”等同于“发明时间”。

句子 (Paragraph D) “During the same period [Tang Dynasty]... tea was served from baskets with multi-coloured paper cups...”

Q3

解析 题目说来自撒马尔罕的造纸工被中国人俘虏了。原文E段说是“a Chinese caravan was captured（一个中国商队被俘虏）”，其中包括造纸工，方向反了，选 FALSE。

干扰 搞清楚谁抓谁，原文是被抓的是中国人（Chinese），被带去撒马尔罕，而不是撒马尔罕人被抓。

句子 (Paragraph E) “...a Chinese caravan was captured which happened to include several papermakers. They were taken away to Samarkand...”

Q4

干扰 “Large-scale industry” 对应原文的 “bulk manufacturing” 和 “important business”。

解析 题目说作为大规模产业的造纸术起源于伊朗。原文E段提到纸张的“bulk manufacturing（批量/大规模制造）”始于伊朗，选 TRUE。

句子 (Paragraph E) “...and bulk manufacturing of paper began in Iran... helped transform papermaking from an art into an important business.”

Q5

解析 题目说造纸技术是通过北非传入欧洲的。原文E段末尾说来自“North Africa（北非）”的摩尔人把技术带到了西班牙和葡萄牙（欧洲），选 TRUE。

干扰 这里的路径是：北非摩尔人 -> 入侵西班牙/葡萄牙 -> 技术进入欧洲。

句子 (Paragraph E) “Finally, when the Moors from North Africa invaded Spain... so it was that papermaking entered Europe...”

Q6

解析 题目说古腾堡发明活字印刷时，纸张材料非常昂贵。原文F段只说这让纸成为实用的日常用品，并未提及当时的纸张价格是否“very expensive”，选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 原文提到以前的羊皮纸（parchment）很贵，也提到后来寻找新材料是因为旧材料（破布）不够用，但没专门说古腾堡时期的纸价。

Q7

句子 (Paragraph F) “Yet soon this source became insufficient and some curious attempts were made to find new materials.”

解析 题目说破布贸易的终结是因为运输困难。原文F段说是因为“source became insufficient（来源变得不足/短缺）”，而不是运输问题，选 FALSE。

干扰 原因归属错误，是“不够用了（insufficient）”，不是“运不过来”。

Q8

解析 题目说植物的____在水中软化，原文A段提到埃及人把植物切成“strips（条/带）”，然后软化，填 strips。

干扰 动词“cut into”后面接的名词即为答案，且符合“softened in water”的动作对象。

句子 (Paragraph A) “The Egyptians cut the plant into strips which they softened in water.”

Q9

解析 题目说羊皮纸由动物如____的皮制成，原文B段提到需要300只“sheep（绵羊）”的皮，填 sheep。

干扰 题目是复数概念（animals such as...），但sheep单复数同形，直接填原词即可。

句子 (Paragraph B) “...required the skins of 300 sheep.”

Q10

解析 题目说皮被干燥并____，原文B段说它们被“stretched（拉伸）”在特殊的框架上，填 stretched。

干扰 寻找与“dried”并列的动作，原文结构是“drying them and they were then stretched”。

句子 (Paragraph B) “The skins had to be specially prepared by drying them and they were then stretched on a special frame.”

Q11

解析 题目说桑树的____和麻布，原文C段提到混合切碎的桑树“bark（树皮）”，填 bark。

干扰 “Of a mulberry tree” 修饰前面的名词，原文是 “mulberry bark”。

句子 (Paragraph C) “...mixing finely chopped mulberry bark and hemp rags with water...”

Q12

解析 题目问751年发生地点，原文E段提到造纸工被带到了“Samarkand（撒马尔罕）”，那里成为了造纸中心，填 Samarkand。

干扰 结合时间“751 AD”和事件（被俘虏带去的地方）。

句子 (Paragraph E) “They were taken away to Samarkand... Samarkand became an important papermaking centre.”

Q13

解析 题目说由____制成的磨坊被使用，原文E段说他们开始在“stone mills（石磨）”中准备纸浆，填 stone。

干扰 题目结构“mills made of ______”对应原文的定语名词“stone mills”。

句子 (Paragraph E) “They began to prepare it in stone mills...”
